title: A Gomory cut in the original variables

blocks.text: A pole-replacement model has whole-number decisions $`x_1, \dots, x_n \ge 0`$ and rows $`A x \le b`$ with integer $`A`$ and $`b`$. Its simplex code adds slack $`s_i = b_i - A_i x`$ to row $`i`$. One row of the optimal tableau, over the columns $`(x_1, \dots, x_n, s_1, \dots, s_m)`$ and the right-hand side, is
with $`r_0`$ fractional. Write the Gomory cut of this row in the model's own variables, so a planner can read it.

Write `gomory_in_x(row, A, b)` in `gomory.py`. `row` is a list of `Fraction`: $`[r_1, \dots, r_{n+m}, r_0]`$. Let $`f(v) = v - \lfloor v \rfloor`$. The Gomory cut is $`\sum_{k=1}^{n+m} f(r_k)\, w_k \ge f(r_0)`$, where $`w`$ is $`x`$ followed by $`s`$. Substitute $`s_i = b_i - \sum_j A_{ij} x_j`$ and return `(g, h)`, two `Fraction` values or lists of them, with

g_j = -f(r_j) + \sum_{i=1}^{m} f(r_{n+i})\, A_{ij} \quad (j = 1, \dots, n), \qquad
h = \sum_{i=1}^{m} f(r_{n+i})\, b_i - f(r_0)
so the cut reads $`\sum_j g_j x_j \le h`$. Return exact fractions; don't scale them.

from __future__ import annotations

from fractions import Fraction
from math import floor


def gomory_in_x(row: list[Fraction], A: list[list[int]], b: list[int]) -> tuple[list[Fraction], Fraction]:
    """The Gomory cut of a tableau row, as  sum_j g_j x_j <= h  in the original variables."""
    n, m = len(A[0]), len(A)
    f = [v - floor(v) for v in row]
    g = [-f[j] + sum(f[n + i] * A[i][j] for i in range(m)) for j in range(n)]
    h = sum(f[n + i] * b[i] for i in range(m)) - f[-1]
    return g, h


if __name__ == "__main__":
    F = Fraction
    print(gomory_in_x([F(1), F(0), F(1, 4), F(1, 2), F(9, 4)], [[2, 1], [1, 3]], [7, 9]))

cases.says: a row with fractional entries under both slacks gives the cut the formula states
with three rows and three slacks, every slack's fractional part is substituted
an entry of -1/5 has fractional part 4/5, since the floor of -1/5 is -1
an original variable with a fractional entry keeps a term of its own in the cut

concepts: the fractional parts of a tableau row give a cut every integer point satisfies
